requirements.section: R-6.1 The pair is the unit
requirements.text: A system reporting the state of a reference MUST report Axis E and Axis A as a pair, together with the time the pair was determined.

requirements.section: R-6.1 The pair is the unit
requirements.text: A system MUST NOT report the state of a reference in a form from which the pair cannot be recovered. A single value is permitted if and only if the pair is recoverable from it; what is forbidden is a value that maps two legitimate pairs differing on one axis onto the same value (Clause 3.4).

requirements.section: R-6.1 The pair is the unit
requirements.text: Where a downstream consumer requires one value, the collapse MAY be performed by that consumer for its own purpose, and MUST NOT be performed by the component that determines the pair.

requirements.section: Good evidence of a past act does not confer present authority
requirements.text: Authorization validity MUST be determined at the time of the decision, not inherited from the evidence of an earlier one.
A pair MUST be determined at a stated time and MUST be recorded with that time.
A pair MUST carry a validity bound stating the period over which the determination is held to apply.

Where the bound has elapsed, the pair MUST be re-determined before it is relied on, or the reliance MUST be reported as being on a lapsed determination. A lapsed determination MUST NOT be reported as current.

A determination is lapsed when the elapsed time since its determination time exceeds its validity bound. A report MUST carry a field that is true if and only if the determination is lapsed at the time of the report.
The bound MUST be declared by the party that determines the pair, and MUST be recoverable by a consumer that did not determine it.
Axis E MUST distinguish at minimum the five values of Clause 3.1.
Where the value is E-verified, the method used MUST be named, and the name MUST identify the method rather than describe it in prose.

A method identifier conforms only if all of the following hold: it contains no whitespace; it is at most 40 characters; and it is not one of the reserved placeholders ``none``, ``n/a``, ``unknown``, ``tbd``, ``hitl``. A name that describes the method rather than identifying it ("verified by hand", "checked against registry") is a description and does not conform.
E-contradicted MUST be reportable as its own value and MUST NOT be reported as a low value on an ordered evidence scale.
E-absent MUST NOT be reported in a form that a consumer would read as an affirmative finding.
Axis A MUST distinguish at minimum the four values of Clause 3.2.
A-revoked and A-expired MUST be distinguishable.
A-suspended MUST be distinguishable from A-revoked, and MUST indicate whether resumption is possible.
Axis A MUST be determined at the time of the decision it supports.
A determination is either **determined** or **unavailable**, and the two are exclusive.
When the reference record cannot be reached, the determination is unavailable. A report MUST NOT present a determined value on one axis and an unavailable marker on the other.
An unavailable determination MUST be reportable as such, and MUST be distinguishable from every determined pair.
A system that cannot reach the reference record MUST report an unavailable determination, and MUST NOT report either axis value.
A decision taken while the record was unreachable MUST be distinguishable, in the record it leaves, from a decision taken on a determination that was available.
Where a system's policy is to proceed or to stop on an unavailable determination, that policy MUST be declared, and the declaration MUST be recoverable from the record of the decision.
Each decision MUST record the version or recency of the pair it consulted.
The record of a decision MUST be sufficient for a party who did not take part in it to establish which version of the pair governed, and at what time.
A change to either axis MUST be observable at the consumer's next consultation, not solely through an event delivered to consumers.
The record of a decision MUST be distinguishable from an acknowledgement that a check was performed. An acknowledgement is not a record of what was consulted.
Re-evaluation MUST be triggered by named events. At minimum: new evidence for the same subject; a change to the version of a policy reference the pair resolves from; elapse of the validity bound.
Re-evaluation MUST NOT depend on the discretion of an operator without a declared criterion.
Where re-evaluation changes a value, both the prior and the subsequent values MUST remain recoverable, with the times at which each applied.

Late-arriving evidence for a subject whose acts have already been decided MUST cause the earlier decisions to be re-examinable. It MUST NOT silently alter the pair in a way that makes the earlier decisions appear to have been taken on the new evidence.

An act under way MUST be bounded, either by a maximum duration or by the continuation points at which it will consult the reference again. Where an implementation cannot bound an act, it MUST declare the act unbounded, and MUST then record the pair in force at every consultation and at termination. An unbounded act is not exempt from R-7.7.2–R-7.7.4; it is subject to them with the consultation points supplied by the implementation rather than by the act.
At each declared continuation point, the act MUST record the pair that governs the following segment, so that the segment assignment is recoverable afterwards.
A change delivered to an act under way MUST be distinguishable, in the record, from a change that arrived after the act ended.

For work fanned out from one act: workers not yet started are separate acts to which the ordinary requirements apply; workers already started are each acts under way and R-7.7.2 applies to each independently; a worker dispatched before a change and begun after it MUST have both facts recoverable — the pair it read itself, and the pair on which its dispatch was decided.

claim.boundary_sentence: A uibc PASS means: within the observed evidence boundary, no violation was detected. It does not claim the agent was correct, safe, or wise; that the recorded inputs were true or complete; or that any real-world outcome followed.
not_claimed: that an untested requirement is unimplementable, or that a tested one is fully covered
that this table is a conformance result for any implementation other than the suite itself
that the count of tests implies the count of requirements covered
